questions.question: What channel structure motivates the paper's use of learned hybrid precoding in mmWave massive MIMO?

options.A: A Saleh–Valenzuela channel with a dominant LOS term and P NLoS paths, whose limited scattering yields low rank
options.B: A dense Rayleigh channel with independent coefficients at every antenna pair
options.C: A frequency-flat channel with no line-of-sight component and full-rank scattering
options.D: A deterministic line-of-sight channel whose rank equals the number of RF chains

questions.rationale: The model sums a LOS component and P scattered paths and points to low-rank structure from limited scattering.
questions.evidence_quote: we introduce the well-known Saleh-Valenzuela (SV) channel model

questions.question: Which constraint distinguishes the analog phase-shifter precoder and combiner in the system model?

options.A: Every analog precoder entry has magnitude 1/√Nt and every analog combiner entry 1/√Nr
options.B: Their entries are binary and each row sums to Ns
options.C: They are unconstrained complex matrices, while only digital stages have constant modulus
options.D: Their Frobenius norms equal the number of antennas

questions.rationale: The analog stages are implemented with phase shifters, imposing fixed-magnitude entries tied to antenna counts.
questions.evidence_quote: all elements of DA and BA are supposed to meet the requirement

questions.question: What sequence of fully connected layer widths and noise-layer width does the proposed DNN use?

options.A: 128, 400, 256, then a 200-unit noise layer, followed by 128 and 64
options.D: 128, 400, 256, then a 64-unit noise layer followed by 200 and 128

questions.rationale: The architecture uses two encoding FC layers, a noise layer, and two decoding FC layers before output.
questions.evidence_quote: two hidden layers for processing encoding operation are also FC layers comprising 400 units and 256 units

questions.question: Why does the paper use a special output activation instead of ordinary ReLU for the network's final layer?

options.A: To enforce the power constraint by clipping each output to [0,Ns]
options.B: To impose constant modulus on the analog precoder
options.C: To produce a unitary decoder through softmax normalization
options.D: To preserve negative-valued complex channel coefficients

questions.rationale: The stated activation clips below zero and above Ns as a power-related bound.

questions.question: What target does the learning loss compare, and what two constraints are placed on the factorized precoder?

options.A: The Frobenius error between R1 and RARD; constant magnitude for RA entries and tr(RARDRH_D RH_A)≤Ns
options.B: BER between transmitted and received bits; unitary RA and orthogonal RD
options.C: The spectral norm between H and RARD; rank-one analog phases and tr(RD)≤1
options.D: The MSE between Q1 and RARD; unconstrained RA and constant-modulus RD

questions.rationale: The loss seeks the GMD precoder R1 through analog/digital factorization, subject to hardware and transmit-power constraints.

questions.question: What batch-size behavior did the BER experiments reveal?

options.A: Larger batches degraded BER, but very small batches risked unstable convergence
options.B: Larger batches improved BER monotonically and accelerated convergence
options.C: Batch size had no effect once the network had 45,000 iterations
options.D: Only batch size 100 converged; all smaller sizes diverged

questions.rationale: The results report a tradeoff between slower convergence at larger batches and instability at very small batches.
questions.evidence_quote: the performance of the deep-learning-based strategy degrades with increasing batch size in terms of BER

questions.question: What tradeoff accompanies lowering the learning rate in the proposed DNN?

options.A: It improves hybrid-precoding BER by reducing validation error but slows convergence
options.B: It worsens BER while making convergence faster
options.C: It has no effect on BER but increases model complexity
options.D: It improves BER and accelerates convergence for all rates

questions.rationale: The paper attributes better performance to lower rates but notes slower convergence and leaves rate selection open.

questions.question: How many iterations did the MSE curves require for convergence for the DNN/sparse schemes versus the analog precoding baseline?

options.A: About 11 iterations for DNN and sparse precoding, versus about 22 for analog precoding
options.B: About 22 for DNN and sparse, versus 11 for analog
options.C: About 45000 for each of the three schemes
options.D: About 11 for DNN only, while both baselines failed to converge

questions.rationale: The MSE comparison reports similar convergence counts for DNN and sparse methods and roughly twice as many for analog precoding.
questions.evidence_quote: both convert at around 11 iterations, whereas the analog precoding scheme requires about 22 iterations.
